chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Riʾāb, from al-Ḥalabī, said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was asked about the wounds of men and women, whether they are equal in retaliation and blood money, so he said:

“Men and women are equal in retaliation: a tooth for a tooth, a head-wound for a head-wound, and a finger for a finger, equally, until the wounds reach one-third of the blood money. Then, when they exceed one-third, the blood money of men regarding wounds is made two-thirds of the blood money, and the blood money of women one-third of the blood money.”

key_terms.الدِّيَاتِ: blood money or financial compensation for injury
key_terms.السِّنُّ: a tooth, mentioned here in retaliatory equivalence
key_terms.الشَّجَّةُ: a wound to the head or face
key_terms.الْإِصْبَعُ: a finger, mentioned as subject to equal retaliation
key_terms.الْقِصَاصِ: legal retaliation in cases of bodily injury
key_terms.ثُلُثَ الدِّيَةِ: one-third of the prescribed blood money threshold
key_terms.دِيَةُ النِّسَاءِ: the blood money assigned to women in this legal context

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on qiṣāṣ and diyah for injuries between men and women in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling on qiṣāṣ and diyah for injuries involving men and women. It establishes equality in retaliatory injury up to one-third of the diyah, after which the compensation for wounds differs according to the stated legal measure.
